[room: gallery alcove | surface: matte limewashed plaster plinth | display: faceless charcoal-velvet half-bust neck-form | accent: single deep-teal note | camera: straight-on eye-level, 10 degrees above | influence: Cereal magazine still-life]
Shot for a Cereal magazine object study. A faceless, featureless charcoal-velvet decollete neck-form rises from a cylindrical limewashed-plaster plinth in a soft seamless alcove, tipped slightly toward camera so the pendant necklace hangs forward in open air rather than flat against the form. One shaft of cool late-morning daylight rakes in from the left, wrapping the metal in graduated highlights with no hard specular blowout, and casting a short soft-edged shadow down the plinth face. The composition sits deliberately off-center, the plinth cropped at the right frame edge, generous negative space above. A single faint lint fibre clings to the velvet near the chain, and a hairline scuff marks the old plaster below. 50mm lens, shallow focal plane on the pendant, far form softening, gentle natural grain in the shadow mid-tones, neutral white balance, a faint subtle reflection of the soft window along the curve of the chain links. A Net-a-Porter campaign frame, airy and premium. A single slim aged-brass T-bar stand rises from a honed pale-grey marble ledge, the pendant necklace draped over its horizontal arm so it hangs completely free in open air and the bright, slightly overexposed window behind lets daylight pass through the chain links, reading them as a clean silhouette. Midday light, neutral and true, with a faint warm bounce off the brass picking up along the chain curve — no mirror-flash hotspots. Only two objects share the surface: the stand and a single small seeded-glass vial set far to the right, half-cropped at the edge, the composition rule-of-thirds and asymmetric. A ghost water ring marks the marble near the base, and one fine dust speck sits on the stone beside, not on, the pendant. 35mm lens, shallow depth so the far vial blurs, micro-contrast on the metal, gentle film grain, 2 percent corner vignette. A Kinfolk overhead flat-lay, shot perfectly perpendicular on a honed dark-slate slab. The pendant necklace lies face-up as the focal point, its chain flowing into a loose, slightly-asymmetric S-curve from a tucked-but-visible clasp — never a symmetric circle. The pendant is lifted a few millimetres on the folded edge of a pale linen swatch so it casts a tiny soft shadow and gains dimension. A single dried eucalyptus sprig lies in soft shadow at the lower left, not crossing the chain — three elements only, odd-numbered and intentional. Diffused overcast skylight from above-left gives graduated wrapping highlights on the metal and one consistent short shadow direction. A couple of fine dust specks rest on the slate beside the piece, and the linen shows a single stray thread. 35mm lens at a believable f/7 look, pendant crisp, swatch edge softening, neutral white balance with no color cast, faint grain.
